title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's notes around the May 1966 letter to Tate. The object is the p-adic Tate module, viewed as a p-divisible group, of an elliptic curve E_K over a complete discretely valued field K with ring of integers A and residue field k of characteristic p. The neighbouring pages sort cases by reduction type: good ordinary, good supersingular (his word 'hypersingulière'), potentially good, and non-integral j (Tate curve).

(1) Top lines: end of case 1° (char K = p). The reading of the first line is uncertain. The case just discussed is an extension of p-divisible groups over K of an étale part by a multiplicative part. Its class lives in a Kummer-type group, roughly the p-adic completion of K^* (tensored with L^{-2}). Such a group maps to Z_p through the valuation K^* -> Z, completed. Classes coming from A land in the completed units A^* (essentially the principal units A^{**}), which have valuation 0. So a nonzero image in Z_p shows the extension does not come from an extension of p-divisible groups over A. Grothendieck then asks what this element of Z_p actually is: a unit, or at least nonzero? This is a computation he leaves open.

(2) Case 2°: char K = 0, char k = p. He remarks that one must study T_p(E_K) as a p-divisible group. In general it can no longer be described purely as a Galois module.

A) Good reduction, ordinary (E_k ordinary). The connected-étale and multiplicative structure of E[p^∞] over A, restricted to K, gives an exact sequence of Galois modules
0 -> Ľ_K ⊗ T_p(G_m) -> T_p(E_K) -> L_K -> 0,
where L_K is a rank-1 unramified Z_p-module and Ľ_K its dual (Weil pairing / det = Z_p(1)). The extension class is not a mere numerical invariant. It is an element of L^{-2} ⊗ A^{**} = Hom(L^{⊗2}, principal units). This is exactly the Serre–Tate parameter q(E) ∈ 1 + m_A (after trivializing L when k is algebraically closed).

The previous page's margin note adds two remarks. The extension can be trivial (q = 1, the canonical lift / CM case), which he flags as contrary to something attributed to Serre. In general the Galois image is abelian. The next page treats non-integral j: Néron model, canonical μ_{p^ν} subgroup, and the class in completed K^* coming from K^*/A^*, i.e. Tate's q-parameter. It also conjectures that E has good reduction iff its p-divisible group does.
errors: The first line is too badly read to be sure which extension (equal-characteristic case) is meant. The argument 'image in Z_p nonzero implies not from A' is correct for the valuation map on completed K^* versus completed A^*. Whether the image is nonzero in the case at hand is exactly what Grothendieck leaves as a question.
No mathematical error visible in the 2°A statement. It matches Serre–Tate theory (class in L^{-2} ⊗ 1+m).

ideas.what: For good ordinary reduction, T_p(E_K) is an extension of L_K by Ľ_K ⊗ Z_p(1), with class in L^{-2} ⊗ A^{**} (principal units); this class can be trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Serre–Tate canonical coordinate q(E) ∈ 1+m; canonical lift when q = 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre–Tate (Woods Hole 1964, unpublished), Lubin–Serre–Tate, Messing; Katz 'Serre–Tate local moduli' (1981)

ideas.what: Extension of étale by multiplicative p-divisible group over K with class in completed K^*; nonzero valuation image in Z_p obstructs extending over A.
ideas.modern_name: Kummer theory for p-divisible groups / Ext(Q_p/Z_p, μ_{p^∞}) ≅ completed K^*; Tate-curve q-parameter
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 (Exp. IX, monodromy/semistable reduction) treats related material

ideas.what: T_p(E_K) in mixed characteristic should be studied as a p-divisible group, not only as a Galois module.
ideas.modern_name: p-divisible groups / Tate's 'p-divisible groups' (1967); precursor of p-adic Hodge theory
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux' (ICM 1970; Montréal 1974)

missed.claim: Explicit open question: identify the element of Z_p attached to the extension class in the equal-characteristic case, and decide whether it is a unit or merely nonzero. This is a small computation, presumably answered implicitly by later work on degenerations and Tate curves in characteristic p.
missed.quote: Question Quel est l'élément obtenu de Z_p ! est-ce une unité, resp. un élément ≠ 0 ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It is likely recoverable from standard Tate-curve / Serre–Tate theory, so it is probably not a genuine gap in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working sketch of known Serre–Tate / Tate-curve structure of Tate modules in the ordinary case, contemporaneous with (or slightly after) Serre–Tate. Historically pleasant, but it contains nothing absent from the later literature.
transcription_corrections: Heading reads '2°) Cas car K = 0 et car k = p'.
'L^{**} ⊗ A^{**}' in the insertion is more likely 'L^{-2} ⊗ A^{**}', consistent with the previous page and the last line.
Line 'Si quand on E_K est ordinaire, donc à réduction ordinaire' is probably 'Si E_k est ordinaire, donc E_K à réduction ordinaire' (the reduction is ordinary).
The struck-out word before 'Il y a lieu d'étudier' is uncertain ('Conclusion' doubtful).
